clue.text: Making a bloomer, phone back about one

indicators.note: going back means the word for phoning is read from its last letter to its first
about means going round, so the turned word wraps itself around the next piece

blocks.note: to phone someone is to call them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone making a blunder after phoning, a bloomer being a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer looks like a gaffe, but here it is something that blooms: a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub is grown for its scented spring blossom, so it is literally a plant that flowers, a bloomer.

clue.text: Lot four includes unusual item-an oft-repeated phrase!

indicators.note: one thing including another holds it inside, so the first word wraps the reworked item
something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, four letters to rearrange
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: An auction listing: lot four contains an odd object, and the catalogue says the same thing over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: IV gives the German spelling LEITMOTIV, not the English LEITMOTIF; the crossing 18 across, VIOLENT, confirms the V.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical theme tied to a character or idea, so loosely any oft-repeated phrase.

clue.text: About sun-up he had to admit defeat

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: A man rising at dawn, forced to concede he was beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Sun-up looks like dawn, but the hyphen hides a reversal: the whole run of letters so far is read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone beaten in a contest, the one who had to concede; the definition describes such a person.

clue.text: A woman's heartless article written after look into plan

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it, so the word for look goes within the plan
without its heart a word loses its middle, keeping only its ends
written after something means set down behind it, so the shortened article comes last

blocks.note: a chart is a map or plan
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
the definite article with its middle letter dropped

explanation.surface: A woman's cold-hearted piece of writing, composed after looking into a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Written after just places the shortened article at the end. Charlotte is a woman's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a common female first name, so the answer names one particular woman.

clue.text: Quite happy just to read when camping

blocks.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read carefully
campers are tented, living under canvas

explanation.surface: Someone on a camping trip happy simply to sit and read.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for read or study is a crossword staple. The word just sits in the surface as filler between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A contented person is satisfied with things as they are, which matches being fairly pleased.

clue.text: The person supplying essentials for the new terrace

indicators.note: a new version of the word is a remade one, so its letters come out in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A supplier bringing basics to a newly built row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Terrace here is a row of joined houses, a common British street layout.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies the food and drink, the essentials of a party or event, to the customer.

clue.text: Report ripped up with speed

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to rip along is to rush, so ripped means ran
rate is speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A report torn to shreds in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripped up wants to mean torn, but ripped is the verb for rushing along, which is turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell or recount events, which is what one does when one reports them.

clue.text: Over-tipped

blocks.note: first meaning: finished, as when the game is over
second meaning: given an end or tip, as a filter-tipped cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes it look like tipping something over; split it, and each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished has come to its close, and an object fitted with a tip has been given an end.

clue.text: Fruit putting real taste into filling before this

indicators.note: something filling another sits inside it, so the short word goes within the next

blocks.note: a tang is a sharp, strong flavour
ere is an old word for before
the preposition reduced to its first part

explanation.surface: Adding genuine flavour to a pie filling before serving.
explanation.walkthrough: Into and this sit awkwardly in this parse, so the printed clue may have lost a word; ERE for before is an old poetic form.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small, loose-skinned orange, a citrus fruit like the mandarin.

clue.text: Put in order for outfit

blocks.note: first meaning: to arrange, as soldiers ... their ranks into line
second meaning: a garment or set of clothes

explanation.walkthrough: Dressing ranks is the military term for straightening a line of troops, which is why the verb means arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to align or arrange neatly, while the noun names clothing, especially a frock.

clue.text: Bringing transient change right away

indicators.note: a change in the word before it means its letters are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A passing shift that takes effect at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare, rather legal adverb from Latin, meaning at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a formal adverb meaning immediately, without delay, so it equals at once in any sentence.

clue.text: Close compact

blocks.note: first meaning: thick or tightly packed, as close fog
second meaning: pressed tightly together, solid

explanation.walkthrough: Close reads like a verb or a word about nearness, but here it is the adjective for something thick, like close or heavy fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe matter packed tightly together with little space between its parts, like thick fog or solid crowds.

clue.text: Married, and said to be virtuous

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
something said is spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A newly married person reported to be of good character.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral person behaves according to good principles, so the adjective matches upright or righteous.

clue.text: Note advertisement on 8, being forward

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
ad is the short form of advertisement
the answer to 8 down

explanation.surface: A memo about an advert placed on page 8, seeming rather pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: Being forward suggests boldness, but forward is the verb for sending post on to a new address.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a letter is to change its address and send it on, just as one forwards mail.

clue.text: The know-all can be pert - it's deplorable

indicators.note: something deplorable is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cocky know-it-all whose cheek is regrettable.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipster sells racing tips, claiming to know which horse will win; the know-all is a playful description of that trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tipster claims inside knowledge of winners, so he is presented as the one who knows everything.

clue.text: Moving after professional encouragement

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the word for moving is placed second

blocks.note: pro is short for professional
motion is the act of moving

explanation.surface: Changing jobs after a word of support from an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the word for moving behind the short form of professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion of a cause or product is active support and furtherance of it, which is a kind of encouragement.

clue.text: Falling in the main

blocks.note: surface reading: mostly falling, as prices falling for the most part
setter's reading: the main is the open sea, and the falling is the water level dropping

explanation.walkthrough: In the main usually means mostly; here the main is the old poetic word for the sea, and what falls in it is the receding water.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebbing of the sea is the period when the water level drops between high and low water.

clue.text: Striking and playing cricket without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cricket word goes around the pause

blocks.note: a side playing cricket at the crease is batting
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A batsman hitting out and playing without any pause.
explanation.walkthrough: Without hesitation suggests decisiveness, but without means outside, so the cricket word surrounds the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Battering is hitting something hard and repeatedly, so it is the act of striking.

clue.text: The canter forming part of a dancer's repertoire

indicators.note: forming something new out of these words means remaking their letters into another shape

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A horse's canter turned into a step in a show performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the feet several times, so it belongs to a dancer's repertoire.

clue.text: Wild flower spreading round the North

indicators.note: something spreading round another thing encloses it, so the flower name wraps the next piece

blocks.note: a small purple spring flower
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A wild plant whose growth is spreading around the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Wild flower reads as one phrase, but Wild is the definition and flower alone is the plant; the model's guess FLORENT is not a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent and wild both describe uncontrolled, ferocious behaviour, as in a wild or violent storm.

clue.text: A holiday-maker who's blundered?

definitions.note: a clause describing a person, standing for one who has blundered

blocks.note: first meaning: a sightseer on a day out
second meaning: one who has stumbled or made a slip

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the word for a day-trip visitor also reads as one who trips up.
explanation.definitionFit: A day trip makes a sightseer a tripper, and anyone who stumbles or slips has tripped.

clue.text: Appeal in French to doctor

blocks.note: en is French for in
to doctor a patient is to treat them

explanation.surface: Making a plea, in French, to a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat someone is to beg or plead earnestly with them, which matches the verb appeal.

clue.text: Some appear confident it lends style

indicators.note: only some letters of the words that follow appear in the answer, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters across these three words

explanation.surface: Self-assurance said to lend a person an air of style.
explanation.walkthrough: Style is the verb meaning to name or give a title to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a title or name, just as to style them is.

clue.text: A game fighter-a good man a champion

blocks.note: taken as written
polo is a game played on horseback
a GI is an American soldier
a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A list of praise for a plucky boxer who is decent and a title holder.
explanation.walkthrough: ST for saint, a good man, is a crossword convention. Champion here is the person who speaks up for a cause, not a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in defence of a belief or person, as a champion of that cause does.

clue.text: Room will be found for the old Greek

blocks.note: first meaning: a space at the top of a house
second meaning: belonging to Attica, the region of ancient Athens

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests finding space for an elderly Greek guest, but the second meaning is the classical dialect and region of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The top-floor room under the roof shares its name with Attica, the ancient Athenian region and its dialect.

clue.text: Exceed expenditure

blocks.note: first meaning: to go further than, surpass
second meaning: money spent, an outlay

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as overspending; as a verb the word means to surpass, and as a noun it means outlay.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to outdo or surpass; as a noun it is spending, the opposite of income.

clue.text: "A lover's eyes will gaze an — blind" (L.L.Lost)

definitions.text: "A lover's eyes will gaze an — blind" (L.L.Lost)

blocks.clueFragment: "A lover's eyes will gaze an — blind"
blocks.note: surface reading: a line of verse with a word left out
setter's reading: fill the gap with the word Berowne uses in Love's Labour's Lost, Act 4 Scene 3

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation with a gap: Berowne claims a lover's gaze could outstare the bird famed for looking straight into the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird was believed able to gaze at the sun undazzled, so a lover outstaring it would make it blind.

clue.text: A great film star's dress-ring

blocks.note: garb is clothing, dress
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A screen legend's gown worn with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Dress-ring looks like one item of jewellery; the hyphen just joins two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish Hollywood star of the 1920s and 30s, one of the screen greats.

clue.text: Oliver's perverted bent

definitions.note: the surname of the Dickens hero Oliver

blocks.note: first meaning: Oliver ... is the orphan hero of the Dickens novel
second meaning: a kink or warped inclination

explanation.surface: A claim that someone called Oliver has a corrupt streak.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver's means the name that belongs to Oliver, his surname in the Dickens title.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist in someone's character is a quirk or warped tendency, and the word also names the Dickens orphan.

clue.text: The leading man

blocks.note: surface reading: the male star of a play or film
setter's reading: the man who leads a family or tribe as its head

explanation.walkthrough: Leading man suggests the theatre; here it is the elder who leads his people, as Abraham did.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family, tribe or church, the man who leads the rest.

clue.text: A meeting about following the correct procedure

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
on course means proceeding as planned

explanation.surface: A gathering held to discuss proper procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: C for circa, about, is a common abbreviation before a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a gathering or coming together of people or things, hence an assembly.

clue.text: Note a lot show spirit here

blocks.note: G is a musical note
a host is a great number, as a host of daffodils

explanation.surface: A rallying call: take note, plenty of you show some spirit here.
explanation.walkthrough: Show spirit sounds like a call for courage; spirit is the definition, a phantom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person, so the noun spirit in its supernatural sense matches.
